title: Plate with hole benchmark (TL × SVK × Hex8/Hex20)
objective: Run the classical plate-with-hole benchmark and confirm the stress concentration factor K_t at the hole edge matches the Kirsch analytical solution (K_t = 3 for a circular hole in a large plate under uniaxial tension).

plan_assets.asset_description: B9.2 plate-with-hole row with Kirsch K_t = 3 reference.

scope: Build a quarter-plate mesh with a circular hole (symmetry on two faces, uniform traction on one far face).
Hole radius << plate half-width (> 10x) for the Kirsch formula to apply.
Extract the peak sigma_xx at the hole edge and compare to K_t * sigma_applied.
Assert K_t computed is within 5% of 3.0 for Hex20, within 15% for Hex8 (coarse).
acceptance_criteria: Hex8 K_t within 15% of 3.0 (documented expected lower accuracy).

cases: Plate with hole Hex8 K_t (coarse baseline)

risks: Stress extraction at the hole edge is sensitive to the quadrature-point location. Mitigation: use nodal extrapolation of the stress tensor rather than per-QP values.
completion_notes: Implemented `mechdsl.verify.benchmarks.plate_with_hole` with a quarter-plate mesh generator, ElementFactory-based TL-SVK benchmark solver for Hex8/Hex20, right-face traction loading, and nodal `sigma_xx` extrapolation at the hole edge.
The benchmark stays within the original task scope: Hex20 reaches K_t ~= 3.1103 (3.68% high vs Kirsch), and Hex8 reaches K_t ~= 2.6621 (11.26% low vs Kirsch coarse-element allowance).
Task-scoped verification passed: `uv run pytest packages/mechdsl-core/tests/test_plate_with_hole.py -v` -> 2/2 passed.

Additional verification passed: `uv run pytest packages/mechdsl-core/tests/test_benchmarks_cook_membrane_matrix.py -v` -> 2/2 passed; `uv run pytest packages/mechdsl-core/tests/test_phase6_exit.py -v` -> 9/9 passed; `uv run mypy packages/mechdsl-core/src/mechdsl/verify/benchmarks` -> success; `uv run ruff check packages/mechdsl-core/src/mechdsl/verify/benchmarks packages/mechdsl-core/tests/test_plate_with_hole.py` -> clean.
